findings: Service rejects START while scanJob.isActive, which narrows earlier state-holder generation concern: normal simultaneous starts are guarded. Cancel requests job cancellation; finally stops foreground, notifies, releases wake lock and stops service. Android lifecycle race behavior remains untested.

Scope include/exclude uses raw startsWith without a path-component boundary. /photos-other/file matches /photos. Missing scope paths are removed from preferences, and an empty valid rule set broadens the request to FULL, including an emptied include list.
Unreadable cache skips files matching path/mtime/size without retrying decode. Once retained, failure can persist after permissions/decoder availability recover without file metadata change.
State Complete is published before saveScanResults. A later persistence exception replaces state with Error, so observers can briefly receive completed data that was not durably saved.
Exact/similar duplicate suppression removes only identical membership sets, allowing overlapping groups to remain. This is source behavior; no duplicate deletion accounting inferred.

Cancellation is checked between major stages, but final state publication follows several side effects without a final explicit ensureActive immediately before setComplete. Subsequent suspend save can catch cancellation and switch to Cancelled while retaining results as defined in holder.
Cleanup operations in finally are sequential without nested try/finally. A notification exception could prevent wake-lock release until timeout/onDestroy; native failure paths not executed.
